topic: Basic tax law within VITA/TCE scope

notes.front: What is a Third Party Designee on a tax return?
notes.back: A person the taxpayer authorises, by checking 'Yes' in that area of the return, to discuss the return with the IRS.
notes.explanation: The designee can be a friend, a family member or another person the taxpayer chooses.
notes.example: Like telling your bank that your brother may ring them about one particular account, and nothing else.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 331
notes.evidence: For taxpayers who want to allow a friend, family member, or another person to discuss their tax return with the IRS, the “Yes” box of the Third Party Designee area of the return can be checked.

notes.front: May a volunteer preparer be named as a taxpayer's Third Party Designee?
notes.back: No, never.
notes.explanation: Publication 4012 repeats the rule: the designee is never the volunteer preparer.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 331
notes.evidence: Volunteer preparers must never be designated as a third party designee.

notes.front: Which lessons of Publication 4491 apply to every certification level?
notes.back: The first six.
notes.explanation: From the Income lessons onward, icons show which level each subject belongs to.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: The first six lessons apply to all levels of certification. Beginning with the Income lessons, the course levels for the subject being covered will be indicated by the following icons:

notes.front: Which publication corrects the 2025 amounts printed in the October 2025 Publications 4012 and 4491?
notes.back: Publication 4491-X, the training supplement (Rev. 1-2026).
notes.explanation: It lists page-by-page changes, for example replacing the printed standard deduction amounts.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Introduction”, PDF p. 4
notes.evidence: This supplement contains changes, revisions, and additions to the October 2025 versions of the VITA/TCE training publications.

notes.front: For 2025, the standard deduction for single or married filing separately is {{c1::$15,750}} (Pub 4491-X corrects the printed $15,000).
notes.explanation: The corrected chart in Publication 4491-X replaces the amount printed in Publication 4012.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page F-3, Standard Deduction”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Single or married filing separate return $15,750

notes.front: For 2025, the standard deduction for married filing jointly or a qualifying surviving spouse is {{c1::$31,500}} (Pub 4491-X).
notes.explanation: The supplement replaces the $30,000 printed in Publication 4012.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page F-3, Standard Deduction”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Married filing joint return or qualifying surviving spouse $31,500

notes.front: For 2025, the standard deduction for head of household is {{c1::$23,625}} (Pub 4491-X).
notes.explanation: The supplement replaces the $22,500 printed in Publication 4012.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page F-3, Standard Deduction”, PDF p. 11
notes.evidence: Head of household $23,625

notes.front: After Publication 4491-X, what is the 2025 limit on the itemized deduction for state and local taxes?
notes.back: $40,000 combined ($20,000 if married filing separately).
notes.explanation: The supplement replaces the $10,000 ($5,000) limit printed in Publication 4012.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page F-11, Entering Schedule A”, PDF p. 13
notes.evidence: The itemized deduction for state and local taxes and sales and property taxes is limited to a combined total deduction of $40,000 ($20,000 if Married Filing Separately).

notes.front: What is the maximum 2025 child tax credit per qualifying child, as corrected by Publication 4491-X?
notes.explanation: The credit calculates automatically in the software once the qualifying child is entered.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page G-5, Child Tax Credit”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: The credit is up to $2,200 per qualifying child and calculates automatically.

notes.front: For 2025, what is the most additional child tax credit a taxpayer can get per qualifying child?
notes.back: $1,700 (Publication 4491-X replaces the $1,400 printed in Publication 4491).
notes.explanation: A taxpayer with more than $2,500 of taxable earned income and a qualifying child may be eligible.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “2025 Publication 4491, page xii: Child Tax Credit/Additional Child Tax Credit”, PDF p. 36
notes.evidence: Under heading Child Tax Credit/Additional Child Tax Credit, in the first sentence, replace, $1,400, with:

notes.front: In Publication 4012, Tab A, which taxpayers does Chart A cover?
notes.back: Most people who must file.
notes.explanation: Anyone who may be claimed as a dependent is sent to Chart B instead.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab A: Who Must File”, PDF p. 35
notes.evidence: Chart A – For Most People Who Must File If you may be claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer, you must file as a dependent whether you are being claimed or not. See Chart B.

notes.front: A person may be claimed as a dependent by a parent. Which Tab A chart decides whether they must file?
notes.back: Chart B, for children and other dependents, whether or not anyone actually claims them.
notes.explanation: What counts is that someone may claim them, not whether anyone does.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab A: Who Must File”, PDF p. 36
notes.evidence: Chart B – For Children and Other Dependents If your parent (or any other taxpayer) may claim you as a dependent, use this chart to see if you must file a return.

notes.front: What does Chart C in Tab A cover?
notes.back: Other situations in which a return must be filed, such as owing special taxes.
notes.explanation: If any condition on the chart applies for 2025, a return is required.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab A: Who Must File”, PDF p. 37
notes.evidence: Chart C – Other Situations When You Must File You must file a return if any of the conditions below apply for 2025. 1. You owe any special taxes,

notes.front: What does Chart D in Tab A cover?
notes.back: Who should file even without a requirement, for example to recover withheld tax or claim the earned income credit.
notes.explanation: The chart goes on to list estimated payments, the earned income credit and other refundable credits.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab A: Who Should File”, PDF p. 38
notes.evidence: Chart D – Who Should File Even if a taxpayer is not required to file a federal income tax return, they should file if any of the following situations below apply. 1. You had income tax withheld from your pay,

notes.front: On the filing status decision tree, how does someone legally separated under a separate maintenance decree answer 'Were you married on the last day of the year?'
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The footnote treats a legal separation under a divorce or separate maintenance decree as not married.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab B: Determination of Filing Status”, PDF p. 51
notes.evidence: Answer “NO” to this question if, on the last day of the year, you were legally separated from your spouse under a divorce or separate maintenance decree.

notes.front: A taxpayer's spouse died during the year and the taxpayer did not remarry. What filing status can they use for that year?
notes.back: They are treated as married for the whole year and can file a joint return with the deceased spouse.
notes.explanation: If they had remarried before year end, they could file jointly with the new spouse instead.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab B: Determination of Filing Status”, PDF p. 51
notes.evidence: If your spouse died during the year, you are considered married for the whole tax year for filing status purposes. If you didn’t remarry before the end of the year, you can file a joint return for yourself and your deceased spouse.

notes.front: To claim a qualifying relative, which dependency table do you start with?
notes.back: Table 1: the person must first pass its dependent taxpayer, joint return and citizen or resident tests (steps 1 to 4).
notes.explanation: Only then do you move to Table 2 for the qualifying relative tests.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab C: Table 2, Qualifying Relative Dependents”, PDF p. 72
notes.evidence: You must start with Table 1. (To claim a qualifying relative dependent, you must first meet the Dependent Taxpayer, Joint Return and Citizen or Resident Tests in steps 1-4 of Table 1)

notes.front: For 2025, a qualifying relative must have gross income of less than {{c1::$5,200}}.
notes.explanation: If the person's gross income reaches that threshold, you cannot claim them as a dependent.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab C: Table 2, Qualifying Relative Dependents”, PDF p. 72
notes.evidence: Did the person have gross income of less than the $5,200 threshold

notes.front: How many digits does an Identity Protection PIN have, and when does the IRS mail it?
notes.back: Six digits, on a notice mailed every December.
notes.explanation: It goes to taxpayers previously identified as identity theft victims, and is entered on the return.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Identity Protection PIN Program”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: Every December, the IRS mails Notice CP01A to taxpayers previously identified as identity theft victims. The notice includes a 6-digit Identity Protection Personal Identification Number (IP PIN) to be entered on the tax return.

notes.front: A taxpayer brings several IP PIN notices. Which IP PIN goes on the return?
notes.back: The most recent one, whatever the tax year of the return.
notes.explanation: Notices keep coming each year while the identity theft indicator stays on the account, usually three years.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Identity Protection PIN Program”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: Taxpayers are mailed Notice CP01A every year as long as the identity theft indicator remains on their account (usually 3 years). Use the most recent IP PIN regardless of the tax year.

notes.front: A taxpayer was issued an IP PIN but did not bring it. What does the site do?
notes.back: Complete a paper return and give a complete copy; to e-file, the taxpayer must bring or phone in the IP PIN.
notes.explanation: Two copies are given if the taxpayer will mail the return.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Identity Protection PIN Program”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: Taxpayer received an IP PIN but did not bring it. 1. Complete a paper tax return for the taxpayer. 2. Provide taxpayer with a complete copy of the tax return. (Provide two copies if the taxpayer will mail the tax return.)

notes.front: Name two ways a taxpayer can get a lost IP PIN?
notes.back: Retrieve it online through an IRS.gov account; or call the IRS to have it reissued by mail.
notes.explanation: The online route requires validating identity; the phone route suits those unable or unwilling to create an account.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Lost, Misplaced, or Non-Receipt of IP PIN”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: If a taxpayer did not receive a new IP PIN or the taxpayer misplaced it, the taxpayer has two options:

notes.front: At which certification levels is Form W-2 wage income in scope?
notes.back: All certification levels.
notes.explanation: Some box 12 codes and some clergy issues are the exceptions.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: F W-2 Yes Wage and Tax Statement All certification levels

notes.front: Which certification does a Form W-2 with box 12 code Q need?
notes.back: Military certification.
notes.explanation: Code Q is listed among the box 12 codes that are otherwise out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Q (Military certification required)

notes.front: Which certification does a Form W-2 with box 12 code W need?
notes.back: Advanced certification.
notes.explanation: Code W is the one box 12 code the chart assigns to Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: W (Advanced certification required)

notes.front: Which Form W-2 earners are out of scope because of issues such as a parsonage or housing allowance?
notes.back: Ministers, and other clergy with issues such as housing allowances or Social Security coverage of their earnings.
notes.explanation: The chart names ministers outright and other clergy when those issues arise.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Other members of the clergy who present issues such as: parsonage/ housing allowance, whether earnings are covered under FICA or

notes.front: Which certification level do tips need?
notes.back: Basic when reported on Form W-2; Advanced for unreported tip income.
notes.explanation: Tips reported on Form W-2 are part of wages; only unreported tip income raises the level.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Wages, salaries, tips, etc. Advanced certification required for unreported tip income

notes.front: When may qualified Medicaid waiver payments be excluded from gross income?
notes.back: Only when the care provider and the care recipient live in the same home.
notes.explanation: If they do not live together, the payments may not be excluded.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Wages, Salaries, and Other Earnings”, PDF p. 91
notes.evidence: Qualified Medicaid waiver payments may be excluded from gross income only when the care provider and the care recipient reside in the same home.

notes.front: Which certification level do interest and dividend income need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes both the question and the Forms 1099 with (B).
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B) Interest or dividends (bank account, bonds, etc.) (B) 1099-INT # (B) 1099-DIV #

notes.front: A taxpayer's only capital gains are capital gain distributions from a mutual fund. Which level can prepare the return?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: No shares were sold, so nothing on this return goes beyond the Basic item.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Interest and Dividends”, PDF p. 98
notes.evidence: A volunteer with a Basic certification can prepare a return with this type of income.

notes.front: When does a state or local income tax refund on Form 1099-G put the return out of scope?
notes.back: When box 3 shows a year other than the preceding tax year.
notes.explanation: A refund for the previous year is in scope and is coded Basic on the intake sheet.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page D-26, State and Local Refund Worksheet”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: The return is Out of Scope if Form 1099-G Box 3 is other than the preceding tax year.

notes.front: Which certification level does unemployment compensation on Form 1099-G need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes unemployment benefits and Form 1099-G with (B).
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B) Unemployment benefits (B) 1099-G #

notes.front: Which certification level does Form 13614-C give Social Security benefits?
notes.back: Basic (B).
notes.explanation: The same line codes railroad retirement benefits (B), but Publication 4012's scope chart requires Advanced for Form RRB-1099, so check the chart for those.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B) Social Security or Railroad Retirement Benefits

notes.front: A pension on Form 1099-R shows its taxable amount, needing no adjustment. Which level can complete the return?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: If the taxable amount is not indicated, an Advanced volunteer generally works it out with the Simplified Method.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 136
notes.evidence: If the taxable amount is indicated and does not need to be adjusted, volunteers with Basic certification can complete the return.

notes.front: Which certification level do disability benefits on Form 1099-R or Form W-2 need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: The intake sheet gives insurance payments and workers' compensation as examples of disability benefits.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B) Disability benefits on 1099-R or W-2

notes.front: Gambling winnings on Form W-2G are in scope. Which gamblers are out of scope?
notes.back: Professional gamblers who use Schedule C.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes gambling winnings, including lottery, as Basic.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Certain Gambling Winnings Not in scope for: • Professional gamblers who use Schedule C

notes.front: Alimony is in scope at Basic. Which divorces are out of scope?
notes.back: Divorces from before 1985.
notes.explanation: The same exclusion applies to alimony received and alimony paid.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: Alimony received, Date of original divorce or separation agreement Not in scope for: • Pre-1985 divorces

notes.front: Which certification level does taxable scholarship income need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: It sits under educational events on page 3 of Form 13614-C.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Taxable scholarship income

notes.front: In which Link & Learn Taxes course is the penalty on early withdrawal of savings taught?
notes.back: The Basic course.
notes.explanation: The Basic course covers wage-earner type returns, including Social Security income and this penalty.
notes.source: Link & Learn Taxes (IRS.gov), “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: Social Security income and penalty on early withdrawal of savings is part of the Basic course.

notes.front: Which certification level does the student loan interest deduction (Form 1098-E) need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: It is an adjustment to income coded (B) on page 3 of Form 13614-C.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Student loan interest (B) 1098-E

notes.front: Which certification level does the educator expenses deduction need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: It covers school supplies bought by a teacher, teacher's aide or other educator.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) School supplies by a teacher, teacher’s aide or other educator (B) Educator expenses deduction

notes.front: Contributions to a retirement account: when are they Basic?
notes.back: When they are to a Roth IRA or a 401(k); deductible traditional IRA contributions need Advanced, and nondeductible ones are out of scope.
notes.explanation: The intake sheet codes the item (B/A) because the level depends on the account; Publication 4012's scope chart splits traditional IRA contributions into deductible and nondeductible.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B/A) Contributions to a retirement account (B/A) IRA (Basic if a Roth IRA or 401K)

notes.front: A taxpayer handed their jury duty pay to their employer, who kept paying their wages. How is the amount handed over treated?
notes.back: As an adjustment to income on Schedule 1.
notes.explanation: The employer continued to pay the taxpayer during jury service, so the handed-over amount is taken off income.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Adjustments to Income”, PDF p. 208
notes.evidence: If the taxpayer turned over any of their jury duty pay to their employer because the employer continued to pay the taxpayer while they served jury duty, include the amount the taxpayer gave their employer as an income adjustment on Schedule 1.

notes.front: Which certification level does the standard deduction need, and which do itemized deductions need?
notes.back: Standard deduction: Basic. Itemized deductions: Advanced.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes the two options (B) and (A).
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Standard deduction (A) Itemized deduction

notes.front: Which certification level does the enhanced deduction for seniors (Schedule 1-A, line 37) need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: The other Schedule 1-A deductions (tips, overtime, car loan interest) need Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 Scope of Service, Schedule 1-A”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: S 1-A 37 Yes Enhanced Deduction for Seniors Basic certification

notes.front: What is the enhanced deduction for seniors, and who can take it?
notes.back: An additional $6,000 for taxpayers aged 65 or older, for tax years beginning before 2029.
notes.explanation: The taxpayer (and spouse if filing jointly) must give a valid Social Security number on the return.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page EXT-9, 2025 Tax Law Changes”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: For tax years (TY) beginning before January 1, 2029, an additional deduction of $6000 for taxpayers Age 65 or older is allowed.

notes.front: Which certification level does the child and dependent care credit (Form 2441) need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: It is out of scope where the taxpayer needs help working out whether employment taxes are owed for household employees.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Child and dependent care (B) Child and dependent care credit

notes.front: Which certification level do education credits need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes the education credit with (B), alongside Form 1098-T.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Education credit or tuition and fees deduction

notes.front: Which education credit situation is out of scope?
notes.back: A taxpayer who must repay (recapture) part or all of an education credit claimed in a prior year.
notes.explanation: Claiming this year's education credits is in scope; recapture of an earlier one is not.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Taxpayers who must repay (recapture) part or all of an education credit claimed in a prior year

notes.front: A taxpayer's EIC, CTC or American opportunity credit was disallowed in an earlier year. Is Form 8862 in scope, and at which level?
notes.back: Yes; the intake sheet codes a previously disallowed credit as Basic.
notes.explanation: The scope chart lists Form 8862 as in scope.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) EITC, CTC, AOTC or HOH disallowed in a previous year

notes.front: Is the retirement savings contributions credit (Form 8880) in scope, and what kind of credit is it?
notes.back: Yes; it is a nonrefundable credit.
notes.explanation: Contributions to a Roth IRA can qualify as well as deductible ones.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Miscellaneous Credits”, PDF p. 273
notes.evidence: The retirement savings contributions credit is a nonrefundable credit eligible taxpayers may claim if they made a qualifying contribution to a retirement plan.

notes.front: Who qualifies for the credit for the elderly or the disabled (Schedule R)?
notes.back: People aged 65 or older, or under 65 and retired on permanent and total disability, with other conditions.
notes.explanation: Schedule R is in scope on Schedule 3, line 6d.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Miscellaneous Credits”, PDF p. 278
notes.evidence: Individuals who qualify for the elderly or the disabled credit are: • Age 65 or older or • Under age 65, retired on permanent and total disability,

notes.front: When can a Basic volunteer handle the foreign tax credit?
notes.back: When Form 1116 is not required.
notes.explanation: If Form 1116 must be filed, the chart requires International or Puerto Rico certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: S3 1 Yes Foreign tax credit Basic certification if See F 1116 for limitations F 1116 is not required

notes.front: Form 1116 must be filed to claim the foreign tax credit. Which certification is needed?
notes.back: International certification (the scope chart also accepts Puerto Rico); Basic and Advanced are not enough.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491 refers these taxpayers to an International-certified volunteer or a professional preparer; Publication 4012's scope chart also names Puerto Rico certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: International or Puerto Rico certifi­ cation required if F 1116 must be filed

notes.front: Which certification level do estimated tax payments, and last year's refund applied to this year, need?
notes.back: Basic.
notes.explanation: The intake sheet asks about both together on page 3 and codes them (B).
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Make estimated tax payments or apply last year’s refund to (B) Estimated tax payments

notes.front: Is the estimated tax penalty (Form 2210) in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The scope chart marks both Form 1040 line 38 and Form 2210 as not in scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: F 1040 38 No Estimated tax penalty

notes.front: Is the earned income credit (Schedule EIC) in scope, and at which levels?
notes.back: Yes, at every level: no certification level is listed.
notes.explanation: If the chart lists no level, the topic is in scope for all certification levels.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: S EIC Yes Earned Income Credit

notes.front: Are the child tax credit and Schedule 8812 in scope, and at which levels?
notes.back: Yes, at every level: the chart lists no certification level.
notes.explanation: Schedule 8812 is filed by everyone claiming the child tax credit, the additional child tax credit or the credit for other dependents.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: S 8812 Yes Credits for Qualifying Children and Other Dependents

notes.front: If the Scope of Service chart lists no certification level for a topic, which volunteers may handle it?
notes.back: Volunteers at every certification level.
notes.explanation: Columns 4 and 5 of the chart can still limit an in-scope topic.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: If no certification level is listed, the topic is in scope for all certification levels.

notes.front: Does a taxpayer have to pay a balance due of less than $1?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: Any larger balance is due in full by the April due date to avoid interest and penalties.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Balance Due Returns”, PDF p. 310
notes.evidence: Taxpayers don’t have to pay if balance due is less than $1.

notes.front: A taxpayer wants the refund split between accounts. Which form is used, and how many accounts are allowed?
notes.back: Form 8888; up to three accounts, in the taxpayer's (or joint-filing spouse's) name.
notes.explanation: In TaxSlayer, Form 8888 is completed inside the e-file section.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Completing the e-File Section”, PDF p. 294
notes.evidence: When the taxpayer elects to direct deposit his or her refund into two or three accounts, you will need to answer additional questions in the e-file section.

notes.front: When is a return in scope with respect to the digital asset question on Form 1040?
notes.back: Only when the taxpayer can check the No box.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers who must answer Yes have digital asset transactions, which are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: In scope if taxpayers can check the No box.

notes.front: A taxpayer only received a digital asset as a gift during the year. How do they answer the digital asset question?
notes.back: No, so the return stays in scope.
notes.explanation: Receiving a digital asset as an inheritance or gift is one of the situations that allows a No answer.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: received digital asset as an inheritance or gift

notes.front: Which certification does preparing the U.S. Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return require?
notes.back: Foreign Student certification.
notes.explanation: It covers, for example, students on F, J or M visas; dual-status individuals are out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: In scope (with Foreign Student certification only) for:

notes.front: Is Form W-7, the application for an ITIN, in scope?
notes.back: Yes.
notes.explanation: The scope chart lists it as in scope with no certification limit.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 10
notes.evidence: F W-7 Yes Application for IRS Individual Taxpayer Identification Number

notes.front: When is Form 1310, claiming a refund due a deceased taxpayer, needed?
notes.back: When anyone other than the surviving spouse files the return.
notes.explanation: It is not needed when a surviving spouse files jointly with the deceased spouse.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 331
notes.evidence: If anyone other than the surviving spouse is filing the return, Form 1310, Statement of Person Claiming Refund Due a Deceased Taxpayer, must be filed.

notes.front: Is Form 8379, Injured Spouse Allocation, in scope?
notes.back: Yes.
notes.explanation: Community property cases are limited by Form 8958's own scope rules.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 20
notes.evidence: F 8379 Yes Injured Spouse Allocation

notes.front: Is Form 8857, Request for Innocent Spouse Relief, in scope?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The scope chart marks it No, unlike the injured spouse allocation.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: F 8857 No Request for Innocent Spouse Relief

notes.front: How long an extension does Form 4868 give a taxpayer living in the United States, and does it extend the time to pay?
notes.back: Six months to file; it does not extend the time to pay.
notes.explanation: Tax not paid by the regular due date carries interest.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 331
notes.evidence: Although taxpayers are not required to pay the amount they estimate as due, Form 4868 does not extend the time to pay their taxes.

notes.front: A taxpayer moves after filing. Where do they send Form 8822, Change of Address?
notes.back: To the IRS service centre for the state where their returns were previously filed.
notes.explanation: The service centre addresses are on page 2 of the form.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 329
notes.evidence: Taxpayers who move after filing a tax return should fill out and mail Form 8822 to the IRS service center based on the state where their returns were previously filed.

notes.front: What checks does Publication 4012 give for a direct deposit routing number?
notes.back: It must have 9 digits and begin with 01 to 12 or 21 to 32.
notes.explanation: Taxpayers should prove the account with a cheque or bank documentation, not a deposit slip.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Pointers for Direct Deposit of Refunds”, PDF p. 308
notes.evidence: The RTN must contain 9 digits and begin with 01 through 12 or 21 through 32.

notes.front: Up to what balance can a taxpayer set up an online payment plan, and when is there no user fee?
notes.back: $50,000 or less; no fee if they can pay within 180 days.
notes.explanation: Longer plans carry an installment agreement user fee, lower for direct debit or online applications.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab K: Balance Due Returns”, PDF p. 311
notes.evidence: If the taxpayer’s balance is $50,000 or less, the taxpayer can make a payment arrangement at Apply Online for a Payment Plan (www.irs.gov/paymentplans). If the taxpayer can pay within 180 days, there is no user fee

notes.front: An older taxpayer trusts her volunteer preparer and asks to name him as her Third Party Designee. What should he say?
notes.back: B: he cannot be named; she could name a family member or friend instead.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, if the site coordinator agrees
B) No, volunteer preparers can never be designees
C) Yes, but only for this year's return
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because the rule has no exceptions: volunteer preparers must never be designated.
notes.explanation: The designee area is for someone the taxpayer chooses outside the site, such as a relative.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Lesson 31: Completing the Return”, PDF p. 331
notes.evidence: Volunteer preparers must never be designated as a third party designee.

notes.front: A part-time student had federal tax withheld from her wages but earned too little to have to file. Which Tab A chart shows she should still file?
notes.back: C: Chart D, Who Should File.
notes.choices:
A) Chart A
B) Chart C
C) Chart D
notes.choicesExplained: Chart A covers most people who must file, and Chart C covers other situations that make filing compulsory. Neither covers someone with no requirement who should file anyway.
notes.explanation: Filing lets her recover the tax withheld.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab A: Who Should File”, PDF p. 38
notes.evidence: Even if a taxpayer is not required to file a federal income tax return, they should file if any of the following situations below apply. 1. You had income tax withheld from your pay,

notes.front: Lena obtained a separate maintenance decree in June and lives alone with no dependants. On the decision tree, what does she answer to 'married on the last day of the year?', and where does that lead?
notes.back: A: No; with no qualifying person, she files as single.
notes.choices:
A) No, leading to single
B) Yes, leading to married filing jointly or separately
C) Yes, leading to head of household
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong because someone legally separated under a separate maintenance decree answers No; head of household would also need a qualifying person.
notes.explanation: The decree changes her answer to the first question on the tree.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab B: Determination of Filing Status”, PDF p. 51
notes.evidence: Answer “NO” to this question if, on the last day of the year, you were legally separated from your spouse under a divorce or separate maintenance decree.

notes.front: Marco supports his father, who lives with him and had $5,300 of taxable pension income in 2025. Can Marco claim him as a qualifying relative?
notes.back: B: no; his gross income is not below $5,200.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because Marco provides his support
B) No, because his gross income is not less than $5,200
C) Yes, because he lives with Marco
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because support and residence do not help if the gross income test fails.
notes.explanation: Each Table 2 step must be passed; failing the income test ends the claim.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Tab C: Table 2, Qualifying Relative Dependents”, PDF p. 72
notes.evidence: Did the person have gross income of less than the $5,200 threshold

notes.front: Sam received an IP PIN this year but left the notice at home. He wants his return done today. What does the site do?
notes.back: A: prepare a paper return; if he wants to e-file, he returns or phones with the IP PIN.
notes.choices:
A) Prepare a paper return, or e-file once he supplies the IP PIN
B) E-file without the IP PIN
C) Turn him away until next season
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the IP PIN must be on an e-filed return issued one. C is wrong because the site can still complete a paper return today.
notes.explanation: The table in Publication 4491 gives a paper return as the first step.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Identity Protection PIN Program”, PDF p. 22
notes.evidence: 4. If taxpayer wants to e-file, arrange for the taxpayer to provide the IP PIN by returning to the site or via telephone.

notes.front: Preparing a prior-year return, Jo has this December's IP PIN notice and last year's. Which IP PIN is used?
notes.back: C: this December's, the most recent.
notes.choices:
A) Last year's, to match the return year
B) Neither: prior-year returns never need one
C) The most recent one
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the most recent IP PIN is used regardless of the tax year. B is wrong because nothing exempts prior-year returns.
notes.explanation: Only the latest IP PIN is valid.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Course Introduction: Identity Protection PIN Program”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: Use the most recent IP PIN regardless of the tax year.

notes.front: A waiter has Form W-2 wages including reported tips, plus cash tips never reported to his employer. What certification does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced, because of the unreported tip income.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because only tips reported on Form W-2 are Basic. C is wrong because unreported tips (Form 4137) are in scope at Advanced.
notes.explanation: The unreported tips set the level for the whole return.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 8
notes.evidence: Wages, salaries, tips, etc. Advanced certification required for unreported tip income

notes.front: A retiree has bank interest and a mutual fund statement showing only capital gain distributions. What is the lowest certification that can prepare the return?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because capital gain distributions alone, with no share sales, are Basic. C is wrong because both items are in scope.
notes.explanation: Advanced would be needed only if shares were sold.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Interest and Dividends”, PDF p. 98
notes.evidence: A volunteer with a Basic certification can prepare a return with this type of income.

notes.front: A taxpayer received unemployment compensation and a Form 1099-G state refund for the previous year. What level does the return need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because both items are coded Basic. C is wrong because a refund is out of scope only when it is for a year other than the preceding one.
notes.explanation: Both kinds of Form 1099-G income are in scope at the Basic level.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B) Unemployment benefits (B) 1099-G # (B) Refund of state or local income tax

notes.front: A retired couple have Social Security benefits and a pension whose Form 1099-R shows the taxable amount. What level does the return need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because Advanced is needed only when the taxable amount is not shown. C is wrong because both items are in scope.
notes.explanation: A shown taxable amount lets a Basic volunteer complete the return.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 136
notes.evidence: If the taxable amount is indicated and does not need to be adjusted, volunteers with Basic certification can complete the return.

notes.front: A graduate student has wages, taxable scholarship income and student loan interest on Form 1098-E. What level does the return need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong: wages, taxable scholarships and student loan interest are all coded Basic.
notes.explanation: None of the three items raises the return above Basic.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Student loan interest (B) 1098-E

notes.front: A saver cashed a certificate of deposit early and paid a penalty on the early withdrawal. Which course covers the adjustment for that penalty?
notes.back: A: the Basic course.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) It is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong because Link & Learn Taxes places the early withdrawal penalty in the Basic course.
notes.explanation: The penalty is an adjustment Basic volunteers are trained to enter.
notes.source: Link & Learn Taxes (IRS.gov), “Course descriptions”
notes.evidence: Social Security income and penalty on early withdrawal of savings is part of the Basic course.

notes.front: A taxpayer contributed to a Roth IRA and wants the retirement savings contributions credit. What level does this need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because contributions are Basic when they are to a Roth IRA or 401(k). C is wrong because the credit (Form 8880) is in scope.
notes.explanation: Deductible traditional IRA contributions would need Advanced.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B/A) Contributions to a retirement account (B/A) IRA (Basic if a Roth IRA or 401K)

notes.front: A homeowner's mortgage interest and state taxes make itemising worthwhile. What level does the return need?
notes.back: B: Advanced.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because only the standard deduction is Basic. C is wrong because Schedule A is in scope with Advanced certification.
notes.explanation: Itemized deductions move the whole return to Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: F 1040 12 Yes Standard deduction or Itemized deductions Advanced certification

notes.front: A 67-year-old with wages and the standard deduction also claims the enhanced deduction for seniors. What level does the return need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the senior deduction is the one Schedule 1-A line at Basic. C is wrong because it is in scope.
notes.explanation: Only the tips, overtime and car loan interest lines of Schedule 1-A need Advanced.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 Scope of Service, Schedule 1-A”, PDF p. 6
notes.evidence: S 1-A 37 Yes Enhanced Deduction for Seniors Basic certification

notes.front: Parents claim the child and dependent care credit for day care and an education credit for a college son. What level does the return need?
notes.back: A: Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Basic
B) Advanced
C) Out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B and C are wrong because both credits are coded Basic on Form 13614-C.
notes.explanation: Recapturing an earlier education credit would put the return out of scope.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 3, Expenses and Tax Related Events”, PDF p. 3
notes.evidence: (B) Child and dependent care (B) Child and dependent care credit

notes.front: A student dropped out after the family claimed an education credit last year, and now part of it must be repaid. Can the site prepare this year's return?
notes.back: C: no; recapture of a prior-year education credit is out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Basic
B) Yes, at Advanced
C) No, it is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because the scope chart excludes taxpayers who must repay part or all of an earlier education credit.
notes.explanation: This is a scope limit, not a certification level.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: Taxpayers who must repay (recapture) part or all of an education credit claimed in a prior year

notes.front: A taxpayer's EIC was disallowed two years ago and the ban has ended. She now qualifies again. Can a Basic volunteer help?
notes.back: A: yes; Form 8862 is in scope and coded Basic.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, with Form 8862, at Basic
B) No, disallowed credits are out of scope
C) Only with Advanced certification
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because Form 8862 is in scope. C is wrong because the intake sheet codes a previous disallowance (B).
notes.explanation: Form 8862 lets the taxpayer claim the credit again after a disallowance.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: F 8862 Yes Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance

notes.front: A Basic volunteer sees foreign tax paid on a Form 1099-DIV. The taxpayer can claim the credit without filing Form 1116. Can the Basic volunteer do it?
notes.back: A: yes.
notes.choices:
A) Yes
B) No, it needs Advanced
C) No, it needs International or Puerto Rico certification
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because Advanced is not the level for this credit. C applies only when Form 1116 must be filed.
notes.explanation: Basic certification covers the foreign tax credit when Form 1116 is not required.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: S3 1 Yes Foreign tax credit Basic certification if See F 1116 for limitations F 1116 is not required

notes.front: A self-employed man underpaid his estimated tax and wants the underpayment penalty worked out on Form 2210. Is it in scope?
notes.back: C: no; the estimated tax penalty is out of scope.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, at Basic
B) Yes, at Advanced
C) No
notes.choicesExplained: A and B are wrong because the scope chart lists the estimated tax penalty and Form 2210 as not in scope.
notes.explanation: Estimated payments are in scope; the penalty for underpaying them is not.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 18
notes.evidence: F 2210 No Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Individuals, Estates and Trusts

notes.front: A taxpayer bought cryptocurrency with dollars in March and has not sold it. Can the return stay in scope?
notes.back: A: yes; purchases with real currency allow a No answer.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, the answer is No
B) No, any digital asset puts it out of scope
C) Only with Advanced certification
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because holding and buying with real currency still allow No. C is wrong because the question sets scope, not a level.
notes.explanation: Only a taxpayer who must answer Yes is out of scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Wages, Salaries, and Other Earnings”, PDF p. 89
notes.evidence: Taxpayers are instructed to check No if they held no digital assets (such as virtual currency or a non-fungible token) for the year or if the taxpayer’s only transactions involving digital assets during the year were a cash purchase,

notes.front: A student on an F visa must file a U.S. Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return. An Advanced volunteer without specialty training offers to help. Is that allowed?
notes.back: B: no; the nonresident return needs Foreign Student certification.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, Advanced covers it
B) No, it needs Foreign Student certification
C) Yes, at any level
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are wrong because the chart puts the nonresident return in scope only with Foreign Student certification.
notes.explanation: Nonresident returns are a specialty certification.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 9
notes.evidence: In scope (with Foreign Student certification only) for:

notes.front: A wife's share of a joint refund was taken for her husband's old student loan. She wants to file an allocation to get her share back. Is it in scope?
notes.back: A: yes; that is Form 8379, the injured spouse allocation.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, Form 8379
B) No, Form 8857 is out of scope
C) No, spouse issues are out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B names the innocent spouse form, which is for a different problem. C is wrong because Form 8379 is in scope.
notes.explanation: Injured spouse and innocent spouse relief are different forms with different scope.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Amended and Prior Year Returns”, PDF p. 344
notes.evidence: When a joint return is filed and only one spouse owes a past due amount such as child support, an education loan, or prior year’s taxes, the spouse who is not obligated for the debt can be considered an “injured spouse.”

notes.front: The printed Publication 4012 says the 2025 standard deduction for a single filer is $15,000; Publication 4491-X says $15,750. Which do you use?
notes.back: B: $15,750, from Publication 4491-X.
notes.choices:
A) $15,000, from the printed guide
B) $15,750, from Publication 4491-X
C) Whichever the software shows, without checking
notes.choicesExplained: A is wrong because the supplement replaces the printed amount. C is wrong because volunteers must review the supplement before preparing returns.
notes.explanation: Publication 4491-X is how the October publications are corrected.
notes.source: Publication 4491-X (Rev. 1-2026), VITA/TCE Training Supplement, “Pub 4012 page changes”, PDF p. 5

notes.front: A Basic volunteer prepares a wage earner's return that claims the earned income credit and the child tax credit with Schedule 8812. Is that within her level?
notes.back: A: yes; both are in scope at every level.
notes.choices:
A) Yes
B) No, the credits need Advanced
C) No, Schedule 8812 is out of scope
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong because the chart lists no certification level for them. C is wrong because Schedule 8812 is in scope.
notes.explanation: A topic with no listed level is in scope for all certification levels.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 15
notes.evidence: S EIC Yes Earned Income Credit

notes.front: For a Form 1099-R, what decides whether the return is Basic or Advanced?
notes.back: Whether the taxable amount is shown: shown, Basic; not shown, Advanced, which works it out with the Simplified Method.
notes.explanation: The intake sheet codes the item (B/A) for this reason.
notes.source: Publication 4491 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Training Guide, “Income – Retirement Income”, PDF p. 136
notes.evidence: In general, if the taxable amount is not indicated, volunteers with Advanced certification must calculate the taxable portion using the Simplified Method covered later in this lesson.

notes.front: How does the foreign tax credit's certification depend on Form 1116?
notes.back: No Form 1116: Basic. Form 1116 required: International certification (the scope chart also accepts Puerto Rico).
notes.explanation: Advanced alone is not enough when Form 1116 is required.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 12
notes.evidence: S3 1 Yes Foreign tax credit Basic certification if See F 1116 for limitations F 1116 is not required International or Puerto Rico

notes.front: What is the scope difference between Form 8379 and Form 8857?
notes.back: Form 8379 (injured spouse allocation) is in scope; Form 8857 (innocent spouse relief) is not.
notes.explanation: The names are similar, but the two forms deal with different problems.
notes.source: Publication 4012 (Rev. 10-2025), VITA/TCE Volunteer Resource Guide, “Scope of Service”, PDF p. 21
notes.evidence: F 8857 No Request for Innocent Spouse Relief

notes.front: How do tips on Form W-2 differ in scope from unreported tips?
notes.back: Tips on Form W-2 are Basic; unreported tips need Advanced and Form 4137.
notes.explanation: Form 13614-C codes tips (B/A) for this reason.
notes.source: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025), Intake/Interview and Quality Review Sheet, “Page 2, Income”, PDF p. 2
notes.evidence: (B/A) Tips (B/A) Tips (Basic when reported on W2)
